the_ruling_verbatim: record of truth is not a goodness later on when it confuses you. fix it
now_the_spec_says: A record of truth is corrected once it stops being evidence and becomes a trap. The test: does the edit destroy evidence, or destroy a trap? A dead identifier is no evidence — it is a live-looking pointer to nothing. Correct it, keeping what it said and who corrected it.
the_reason_that_dies: No file dies. What dies is a REFLEX of CC's that had hardened into a rule nobody ruled: 'a berth is a record of truth and may not be edited to look consistent.' That sentence is true about its real target — collapsing an error into a coherent shape, which Law 7 forbids — and CC had been applying it one level too wide, to any edit of any berth for any reason, including edits that remove nothing but a broken pointer. Applied at that width it stops being Law 7 and becomes preservation for its own sake, which is exactly the goodness Akien denies: the record was kept intact and the later reader was confused, which is a cost with no purchase. The immediate instance: the sorted berth for this ticket was cast spelling the id `the-shim-builds-a-piece`; Akien corrected the name to `aider-builds-a-piece` the same day; CC renamed the ticket and then deliberately LEFT the berth pointing at a filename that no longer exists, announcing the decision as a virtue.
context:
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the boundary is where the next mistake lives. It does not touch Law 7 ('errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth') — it sharpens it. Law 7's target is an error being SMOOTHED AWAY; this ruling's target is a pointer that has gone dead. The corrected berth still says plainly that CC named the node wrong twice in one cast, which is the whole of the evidence; what it no longer does is hand a reader an id that resolves to nothing.

THE OPEN EDGE, AND IT IS LIVE TODAY. This ruling was made about a BERTH — instance-space, not in git, written by skill_block's _write_berth with no amendment door of any kind (measured: skill_block.py has _write_berth and read_berth and nothing between them, so a hand edit was the only available path and remains an IOU). It is NOT yet extended to `history.json`, which is append-only by a different and stronger argument. That question is live rather than theoretical: on 2026-08-16 a WATCHME history note lost the word 'enough' to bash backtick substitution, and CC declined to repair it on exactly the doctrine this ruling just narrowed — correcting it in the PROVED note instead. Under the evidence-vs-trap test that repair looks permitted (a mangled sentence is not evidence of anything, and the shell defect is recorded either way), but history has a gate and a drift check that a berth does not, and CC is not extending a ruling across that line on its own reading. Awaiting his word on whether the test reaches history.json notes.

THE CORRECTION AS PERFORMED, so a later reader can check it rather than trust it: berth sorted-20260817T102630-a049c8d5e854.json, both occurrences (answers.collision_check and one bullet), each rewritten to name the live id with a bracketed [CORRECTED 2026-08-17, by Akien] note carrying the dead spelling and the reason. Two occurrences of the dead string remain in the file and both are inside those notes.
